scope.description: A node in the captured module that installs an InstallSnapshotRequest whose snapshot was produced by a leader that had committed and applied through the snapshot index, observed before any later AppendEntries advertises a commit index.
assumptions: the installed snapshot carries entries the source had committed and applied, which is what the source's own Snapshot API produces
the receiving node's last index after the install is the snapshot index, so no legal commit index exceeds it
excluded: the correctness of the snapshot payload itself, which the check does not inspect
the configuration carried by the snapshot
behaviour after a later AppendEntries has advanced the value
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: No target file is modified; the harness adds one external test file to the captured package.

The snapshot is produced by a real single-voter leader through the public Snapshot API and is opened from that node's own SnapshotStore, so the installed index is an index the source reported as committed and applied.

The InstallSnapshot request is built from that snapshot's metadata and delivered through the module's own InmemTransport InstallSnapshot method, so installSnapshot, its sink handling, the FSM restore path and the log truncation are the target's own code.

Only the InstallSnapshot RPC is routed from the source transport to the receiver, and the receiver's election timeouts are long, so neither AppendEntries nor an election changes the receiver inside the observed prefix.

plan_uncertainties: The prefix observes the receiver before any later AppendEntries, so it does not measure how long the value stays low in a live cluster; a live follower would have its commit index advanced by the next heartbeat, while a node restarted from a snapshot keeps the low value until a leader contacts it.
The observable is an index value rather than a state transition, so the check reports what the node published rather than a downstream consequence for a caller.

The receiver's cluster contains two voters while the source produced the snapshot as a single-voter leader; the configuration carried by the snapshot is not read by the requirement under test, but the difference is recorded here.
grounding_unresolved: whether the published value is intentionally limited to the leader's last advertised commit index, which no source states
whether any consumer depends on the value on a follower
whether the startup restore path shares the same requirement or needs its own scenario
whether the library intends the follower's published commit index to be strictly the value the leader last advertised, which would make the omission deliberate rather than a defect
whether the intended repair advances the commit index inside installSnapshot or derives the published value from the last snapshot index
whether the same omission on the startup restore path (api.go restoreSnapshot) should be treated as one requirement or a second entry point
whether a later AppendEntries in a live cluster advances the value before a caller could read it, which this prefix does not produce
